types.name: GlobalID
types.description:
A global identifier.

A global identifier represents an object uniquely across the application.
An example of a global identifier is `"gid://gitlab/User/1"`.

`gid://gitlab` stands for the root name.
`User` is the name of the ActiveRecord class of the record.
`1` is the record id as per the id in the db table.

Global identifiers are encoded as strings.

enumValues.description: The Planner role is suitable for team members who need to manage projects and track work items but do not need to contribute code.

enumValues.name: REPORTER
enumValues.description: The Reporter role is suitable for team members who need to stay informed about a project or group but do not actively contribute code.

enumValues.name: SECURITY_MANAGER
enumValues.description: The Security Manager role is for security team members who need to view and manage security features for the group or project.

enumValues.name: DEVELOPER
enumValues.description: The Developer role gives users access to contribute code while restricting sensitive administrative actions.

enumValues.name: MAINTAINER
enumValues.description: The Maintainer role is primarily used for managing code reviews, approvals, and administrative settings for projects. This role can also manage project memberships.

enumValues.name: OWNER
enumValues.description: The Owner role is typically assigned to the individual or team responsible for managing and maintaining the group or creating the project. This role has the highest level of administrative control, and can manage all aspects of the group or project, including managing other Owners.

enumValues.name: MINIMAL_ACCESS
enumValues.description: The Minimal Access role is for users who need the least amount of access into groups and projects. You can assign this role as a default, before giving a user another role with more permissions.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_AI_CATALOG_ITEM_CONSUMER
enumValues.description: Enable, disable, and configure custom agents and flows from the AI catalog for a project.

enumValues.name: REMOVE_GROUP
enumValues.description: Ability to delete or restore a subgroup. This ability does not allow deleting top-level groups. Review the retention period settings to prevent accidental deletion.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_AI_CATALOG_ITEM
enumValues.description: Create, edit, and delete custom agents and flows in the AI catalog.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_COMPLIANCE_FRAMEWORK
enumValues.description: Create, read, update, and delete compliance frameworks. Users with this permission can also assign a compliance framework label to a project, and set the default framework of a group.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_CICD_VARIABLES
enumValues.description: Create, read, update, and delete CI/CD variables.

enumValues.name: MANAGE_DEPLOY_TOKENS
enumValues.description: Manage deploy tokens at the group or project level.

enumValues.name: MANAGE_GROUP_ACCESS_TOKENS
enumValues.description: Create, read, update, and delete group access tokens. When creating a token, users with this custom permission must select a role for that token that has the same or fewer permissions as the default role used as the base for the custom role.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_GROUP_MEMBER
enumValues.description: Add or remove users in a group, and assign roles to users. When assigning a role, users with this custom permission must select a role that has the same or fewer permissions as the default role used as the base for their custom role.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_INTEGRATIONS
enumValues.description: Create, read, update, and delete integrations with external applications.

enumValues.name: MANAGE_MERGE_REQUEST_SETTINGS
enumValues.description: Configure merge request settings at the group or project level. Group actions include managing merge checks and approval settings. Project actions include managing MR configurations, approval rules and settings, and branch targets. In order to enable Suggested reviewers, the "Manage project access tokens" custom permission needs to be enabled.

enumValues.name: MANAGE_PROJECT_ACCESS_TOKENS
enumValues.description: Create, read, update, and delete project access tokens. When creating a token, users with this custom permission must select a role for that token that has the same or fewer permissions as the default role used as the base for the custom role.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_PROTECTED_BRANCH
enumValues.description: Create, read, update, and delete protected branches for a project.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_PROTECTED_ENVIRONMENTS
enumValues.description: Create, read, update, and delete protected environments

enumValues.name: ADMIN_PUSH_RULES
enumValues.description: Configure push rules for repositories at the group or project level.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_RUNNERS
enumValues.description: Create, view, edit, and delete group or project Runners. Includes configuring Runner settings.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES
enumValues.description: Manage the security categories and attributes belonging to a top-level group. Also requires the `read_security_attribute` permission.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_TERRAFORM_STATE
enumValues.description: Execute terraform commands, lock/unlock terraform state files, and remove file versions.

enumValues.name: ADMIN_VULNERABILITY
enumValues.description: Edit the status, linked issue, and severity of a vulnerability object. Also requires the `read_vulnerability` permission.

enumValues.name: READ_COMPLIANCE_DASHBOARD
enumValues.description: Read compliance capabilities including adherence, violations, and frameworks for groups and projects.

enumValues.name: READ_VIRTUAL_REGISTRY
enumValues.description: Allows read access to virtual registries at the group level. Enables users to resolve packages through the virtual registry without requiring broader group membership permissions. Only works on top level groups.

enumValues.name: UPDATE_SEC_AI_WORKFLOW_SETTINGS
enumValues.description: Update security AI workflow settings such as SAST Vulnerability Resolution. Also requires the `read_vulnerability` permission.

enumValues.name: READ_ADMIN_CICD
enumValues.description: Read CI/CD details for runners and jobs in the Admin Area.

enumValues.name: READ_DEPENDENCY
enumValues.description: Allows read-only access to the dependencies and licenses.

enumValues.name: READ_ADMIN_GROUPS
enumValues.description: Read group details in the Admin Area.

enumValues.name: READ_ADMIN_PROJECTS
enumValues.description: Read project details in the Admin Area.

enumValues.name: READ_CODE
enumValues.description: Allows read-only access to the source code in the user interface. Does not allow users to edit or download repository archives, clone or pull repositories, view source code in an IDE, or view merge requests for private projects. You can download individual files because read-only access inherently grants the ability to make a local copy of the file.

enumValues.name: READ_RUNNERS
enumValues.description: Allows read-only access to group or project runners, including the runner fleet dashboard.

enumValues.name: READ_SECURITY_ATTRIBUTE
enumValues.description: Allows read-only access to the security categories and attributes that belong to a top-level group.

enumValues.name: READ_ADMIN_SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Read subscription details in the Admin area.

enumValues.name: READ_ADMIN_MONITORING
enumValues.description: Read system information such as background migrations, health checks, and Gitaly in the Admin Area.

enumValues.name: READ_ADMIN_USERS
enumValues.description: Read the user list and user details in the Admin area.

enumValues.name: READ_VULNERABILITY
enumValues.description: Read vulnerability reports and security dashboards.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION

enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: VARIABLE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a variable definition.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name and description, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields` and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

args.description: Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion for how to access supported similar data. Formatted in [Markdown](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/).

directives.description: Marks a field as introduced in a specific version. Fields with a version higher than the current one will return null.

args.description: The version when this field was introduced (e.g. '18.1.0')

args.name: permissions
args.description: Granular scope permissions required to access the field or type.

args.name: boundaryType
args.description: The type of authorization boundary (project, group, user, instance). Used for validation and documentation of the permission boundary.

args.name: boundary
args.description: Method name to call on the resolved object to extract the authorization boundary (Project/Group). Use when the object is already resolved (fields on types, nested fields).

args.name: boundaryArgument
args.description: Argument name containing the authorization boundary (path or GlobalID). Use for mutations and query fields where the boundary is passed as an argument.

args.name: traversal
args.description: When true, this directive only verifies the token is scoped to the boundary (read_boundary), without enforcing the listed permissions. Use for entry-point fields like Query.group(fullPath:) where downstream fields enforce the real permissions. Only applies to project and group boundary types. All other boundary types fall back to the regular permission check.
